title: Automated Phase and Orientation Mapping of Complex Multiphase Samples using 4DSTEM and Precession Electron Diffraction
content: Accurate determination of crystal orientation and phase distributions in polycrystalline materials is critical for understanding structure-property relationships in many materials, including polycrystalline thin films, metallic alloys, nanoparticle assemblies, geological minerals, and others. We can use four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) to record thousands or even millions of diffraction patterns, which act as fingerprints for the local crystal structure [1]. To achieve high spatial resolution while also sampling enough crystal grain unit cells to maintain high sensitivity to crystal orientation, we use intermediate probe convergence angles, known as nanobeam electron diffraction. We can further improve orientation sensitivity by tilting the beam around a small-angle cone of incidence angles relative to the sample surface and averaging the resulting diffraction patterns, a method known as precession electron diffraction (PED) [2]. Modern 4DSTEM experiments can however produce very large datasets, which therefore require robust, efficient, and ideally automated software methods to analyze.
